name: The Salvation Army USA: overseas work (charityevals' estimate)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: the World Service Office's grants and the territories' support for the international Salvation Army; SAWSO lists the 69 countries it funded in fiscal 2025 and publishes no split, so they share equally (a judgment).
summary: The Salvation Army USA's overseas work, about 1% of its programme spending ($39.7 million in fiscal 2025): the World Service Office's grants to Salvation Army units in 69 countries for disaster relief (mostly Ukrainian refugees), livelihoods (savings groups and income generation), education, health and anti-trafficking, and its and the territories' operating support for poorer territories, three-quarters of the money. SAWSO publishes no count of people reached or of outcomes, so every branch is built from the research on its kind of work (savings-group trials, the Cochrane review of community newborn care, the median effect of education programmes, studies of what relief costs to deliver) with its own spending, and every branch is discounted for missing data; the operating support is valued at what the services it pays for cost, at poor households' consumption. It comes to about 0.09 years of healthy life per $1,000, some 25 times the US work per dollar, because a dollar does far more on the log scale for a poor household, but far below the site's global-health median: the money is spread over church running costs and small projects with no measured effect, valued at about what it costs. The biggest uncertainties are whether savings groups raise consumption at all (the largest trial found no effect), what the operating support becomes and what it is worth, and the size of the territories' support, which isn't published.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.explainer: The shared Salvation Army figure (facts/salvation_army.json), read by this model and by the US model. The combined statement of the six US corporations; the overseas work is paid through them.

rows.explainer: As in the US model: the rehabilitation line less the recovery programme, paid by the stores' sales, not by donors.

rows.label: Day-care fees (out of both totals)

rows.label: Overseas work paid through the US accounts, fiscal 2025
rows.formula: relief_spend + livelihood_spend + education_spend + health_spend + trafficking_spend + support_spend
rows.explainer: The World Service Office's fiscal-2025 programmes by sector (its annual report, p. 20) and the territories' other support for the international Salvation Army (a judgment, facts/salvation_army.json). About 1% of the US programme spending. Every line is a branch below.

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ programme expenses)
rows.explainer: The US Salvation Army's management and fundraising spread over all its programmes in proportion to their cost, with the thrift stores' running costs and day-care fees out of both totals, exactly as in the US model: the overseas work is raised by the same kettles and appeals. SAWSO's own support services ($1.08M) are inside the national management line.

rows.label: Cost of the overseas work, including overhead
rows.explainer: Programme spending times the overhead multiplier.

rows.label: Disaster relief and recovery, fiscal 2025 (the main branch: the canonical rows)
rows.explainer: The shared Salvation Army figure (facts/salvation_army.json), read by this model and by the US model.

rows.label: Share of relief spending that reaches people as goods, vouchers or services
rows.explainer: Judgment 70% (50-85%). The rest is procurement, transport, staff and monitoring. Anchors: activity-based costings of transfers in Ecuador, Niger, Uganda and Yemen found every cash transfer cheaper to deliver than food (Margolies & Hoddinott 2015, Journal of Development Effectiveness, doi:10.1080/19439342.2014.984745), and the Campbell review ranks cost per beneficiary cash < vouchers < in-kind food (Doocy & Tappis 2017, doi:10.4073/csr.2017.17). SAWSO's fiscal-2025 relief was mostly grocery vouchers and goods for Ukrainian refugees, between the two.

rows.label: What a dollar of goods or vouchers is worth to the family, against a dollar of cash
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%). Vouchers and goods restrict choice; comparative trials of cash and food in ten countries find their effects on consumption similar on average (Gentilini 2016, World Bank, doi:10.1596/978-1-4648-0910-1; Gentilini 2015, World Bank Research Observer), and grocery vouchers in shops are close to cash.

rows.label: People helped by the relief (implied)
rows.explainer: Relief spending reaching people, at its cash value, over the value each person got. SAWSO publishes no count of people its fiscal-2025 grants reached, so reach is implied by spending; on the log scale a small gift's value is almost proportional to its size, so the split into people barely moves the result.

rows.label: Cost per person helped by the relief (with overhead)
rows.explainer: The relief branch's own cost, with overhead, per person reached; the other branches have their own reach rows.

rows.label: Livelihoods projects, fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The shared Salvation Army figure (facts/salvation_army.json), read by this model and by the US model.

rows.label: Cost per savings-group or livelihood-project member
rows.explainer: Judgment $40 ($20-100) in today's dollars. Anchor: CARE's savings-group programme in the three-country trial cost $26 per member in Malawi and $20 in Uganda over 22 months (2011 dollars, central and operational costs), and vsla.net gives $22 as the global average (Karlan, Savonitto, Thuysbaert & Udry 2017, PNAS, doi:10.1073/pnas.1611520114, p. 6); SAWSO's livelihoods also fund income generation and agriculture, which cost more per person, and its projects are small.

rows.label: Members reached by the livelihoods projects (implied)
rows.explainer: Spending over the cost per member: SAWSO publishes no count.

rows.label: People per member's household
rows.explainer: The average of the site's household sizes for the rural places where savings-group trials ran and SAWSO works (@household_size.malawi_rural, uganda_rural, kenya_rural, bangladesh_rural, india): a member's whole household shares a consumption gain.

rows.label: Education projects, fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The shared Salvation Army figure (facts/salvation_army.json), read by this model and by the US model.

rows.label: Cost per child reached for a year
rows.explainer: Judgment $150 ($50-500). The projects are small: preschools upgraded in 11 Rwandan communities (more than 300 children now in preschools meeting the standards), four community learning centres in the Republic of the Congo, a nursing dormitory for 96 students in Indonesia (SAWSO annual report 2026, pp. 12-17). Building work makes the first year's cost per child high; a nursing student costs far more than a preschooler.

rows.label: Children and students reached (implied)
rows.explainer: Spending over the cost per child.

rows.label: Health projects, fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: The shared Salvation Army figure (facts/salvation_army.json), read by this model and by the US model.

rows.label: Cost per birth covered by community maternal and newborn care
rows.explainer: Judgment $100 ($30-400). The trials' packages (home visits in pregnancy and after birth, community mobilisation, clean delivery) cost tens of dollars per birth at scale; SAWSO's health grants run through Salvation Army clinics and health programmes, smaller and with buildings and training to pay for.

rows.label: Births covered (implied)
rows.explainer: Spending over the cost per birth: SAWSO publishes no count.

rows.label: Operating support for Salvation Army territories abroad, fiscal 2025
rows.explainer: SAWSO's mission support and business-development grants (income-earning assets such as solar panels that free a unit's budget) and the territories' world-services support to International Headquarters, which distributes it by need to territories that can't pay their own way. Read from the shared facts.

rows.label: Share of the supported territories' spending that delivers social, health and education services
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (25-75%). The money pays for the territories' running costs as a whole (officers, buildings, administration, IT): it funds their worship and community centres (corps) as well as their schools, clinics, hospitals and social services. The international Salvation Army reports almost 15,000 corps worldwide beside about 2,400 schools and kindergartens and some hundred hospitals and many clinics (Salvation Army Year Book statistics), most of the schools and health services in the territories this money supports. The worship share is not valued here (see unmodelled benefits).

rows.label: What a dollar of these services is worth to the people served, against a dollar of cash
rows.explainer: Judgment 50% (20-100%). No study measures what these services are worth. A dollar of operating support passes through administration and buildings before it becomes a lesson, a consultation or a meal, and in poor countries people value services below their cost when they must pay (demand falls steeply with price: Kremer & Holla 2009, Annual Review of Economics); the top of the range takes the services as worth their full cost.

rows.label: People served by the supported services (implied)
rows.explainer: The services' cash value over the value each person got.

rows.label: Death rate of the people reached during the crisis (per person-year)
rows.explainer: Judgment 1.2% (0.9-2%). Most of fiscal 2025's relief went to Ukrainian refugees in Bulgaria, Moldova, Romania and Georgia and to people inside Ukraine, an old population (Ukraine's crude death rate is about 1.5-1.8% a year in recent UN estimates) where war adds deaths near the front but little among refugees abroad.

rows.label: Death rate the same people would have had without the crisis (per person-year)
rows.explainer: Judgment 1.1% (0.8-1.5%): the countries' normal crude death rates for an older population.

rows.label: Share of the excess deaths the relief averts for the people reached
rows.explainer: Judgment 5% (0-20%). Grocery vouchers and goods for refugees housed in host countries relieve hardship; they are not the nutrition, water or medical relief that averts deaths in a famine or epidemic.

rows.label: Years each person is helped
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.25 (0.1-0.5): vouchers and parcels for a few months.

rows.label: Deaths averted per person reached
rows.explainer: Excess mortality × share averted × years.

rows.label: Share of averted deaths under five
rows.explainer: Judgment 5% (0-15%): in an old European population few deaths are of young children.

rows.label: Share aged 5-14 among deaths over five
rows.explainer: Judgment 2% (0-10%): school-age children are a small share of deaths in an old population; 10% if more of the relief reached families with children in Ukraine.

rows.label: Share aged 15-49 among deaths over fifteen
rows.explainer: Judgment 15% (5-35%): most deaths in Ukraine's population are of older people.

rows.label: Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The shared values by age band (@moral_weights) × $life_value_multiplier.

rows.label: Illness averted per person (DALYs)
rows.explainer: 0: vouchers and goods for refugees aren't health care; any health gain is inside the small share of deaths averted.

rows.label: Cash value of the relief each person got
rows.explainer: Judgment $80 ($30-250): a few months of grocery vouchers and essential items per person in a refugee household.

rows.label: Price-level step (1: both sides in market dollars)
rows.explainer: 1: the value delivered and the people's consumption below are both in current US dollars at market rates, so the ratio needs no PPP step (with both in PPP dollars it would be the same ratio).

rows.label: Consumption per person of the people the relief reached (current US$ a year)
rows.explainer: Judgment $2,500 ($1,000-6,000). Refugee and displaced households from Ukraine living on low wages or benefits in Bulgaria, Moldova, Romania and Georgia, and people inside Ukraine near the front: far below their host countries' averages, far above the world's poorest (the site's Bangladesh figure is $1,819, @bangladesh.consumption_per_person_2024, for reference).

rows.label: Gain in ln(consumption) per person
rows.explainer: The relief's cash value over a year's consumption, on the site's log scale.

rows.label: Consumption gain per member household, share of consumption
rows.explainer: Judgment +1% (-3% to +5%). The three-country trial of CARE's savings groups (15,000 households in Ghana, Malawi and Uganda) found no effect on consumption: -0.6 dollars a person a month (SE 0.75) against a control mean of 35.7, for villages offered groups, of which about a third of households joined (Karlan et al. 2017, PNAS, Table 1), i.e. about -5% ± 7% per member household; it found better business outcomes and women's empowerment. A Malawi trial found more meals and higher spending (Ksoll et al. 2016, Journal of Development Economics, doi:10.1016/j.jdeveco.2015.12.003), the Mali trial better food security but no higher spending (Beaman, Karlan & Thuysbaert 2014, NBER w20600), and a re-analysis of the Uganda and Malawi trial found 23-28% of the benefits went to neighbouring villages (Heitzig et al. 2023, World Development). A small positive gain, with a range that includes harm.

rows.label: Years the gain lasts
rows.explainer: Judgment 2 (1-4): the trials measured 2-3 years after groups began; groups often keep running, gains from a new business fade.

rows.label: Gain in ln(consumption) per person, discounted over its years
Learning gain per child (standard deviations)

source.title: Evans & Yuan (2022), How Big Are Effect Sizes in International Education Studies?, Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis, doi:10.3102/01623737221079646
source.quote: We identify a median effect size of 0.10 standard deviations on learning and 0.07 standard deviations on access among randomized controlled trials.

rows.explainer: The median effect on learning of 234 randomized and quasi-experimental studies of education programmes in low- and middle-income countries, 0.10 SD (larger, and more variable, in small studies such as these); the range runs from school-management programmes (0.03 SD, Anand et al. 2023) to teacher-training and pedagogy programmes (0.12-0.3 SD: McEwan 2015, Conn 2017).

rows.label: Earnings gain per SD of learning that lasts into adult life
rows.explainer: Judgment 20% (10-40%). A year of schooling raises earnings about 9% (Psacharopoulos & Patrinos 2018, Education Economics, doi:10.1080/09645292.2018.1484426, 1,120 estimates in 139 countries; about 10% in causal estimates, Patrinos et al. 2026), and a school year in poor countries adds well under one SD of learning, so an SD of lasting learning is worth more than a year's return; adult test-score studies put it at 10-20% of earnings.

rows.label: Share of the learning gain still there in adult life
rows.explainer: Judgment 40% (20-80%): effects of education programmes fade in the years after them, more for preschool and short programmes.

rows.label: Years from the programme to adult earnings
rows.explainer: Judgment 12 (6-16): preschoolers and primary-age children start work 12-15 years later, nursing students in 2-4.

rows.label: Years the earnings gain lasts
rows.explainer: The site's shared working life for later-life income gains (@givewell_shared.long_term_benefit_years).

rows.label: People who share a worker's income gain
rows.explainer: The site's shared figure for later-life income gains (@givewell_shared.resource_sharing_multiplier), as in every model of them.

rows.label: Gain in ln(consumption) per child reached, discounted to today
rows.formula: ln(1 + education_learning_gain_sd * education_earnings_per_sd * education_persistence) * pv_annuity_due(1, $discount_rate, education_working_years) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ (0 - education_years_until_work) * education_resource_sharing
rows.explainer: ln(1 + learning gain × earnings per SD × persistence) for each working year, discounted, after the wait to adult work, shared with the household.

rows.label: Neonatal mortality where the health projects run (deaths per live birth)
rows.explainer: Judgment 2.2% (1.2-3%): UN IGME puts neonatal mortality at about 27 per 1,000 in sub-Saharan Africa and 23 in South Asia, lower in Latin America; SAWSO's health work is mostly in Africa and Asia.

rows.label: Relative risk of neonatal death with community maternal and newborn care packages

source.title: Lassi & Bhutta (2015), Community-based intervention packages for reducing maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality and improving neonatal outcomes, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, doi:10.1002/14651858.CD007754.pub3
source.quote: neonatal mortality (average RR 0.75; 95% CI 0.67 to 0.83; 21 studies, n = 302,646

rows.explainer: The Cochrane review of 26 cluster-randomised and quasi-randomised trials, random effects; the confidence interval as the range. Applied to SAWSO's health grants as the closest trialled kind of community health work; the fit is in health_evidence_adj.

rows.label: Stillbirths per birth where the projects run
rows.explainer: Judgment 1.7% (0.8-2.5%): UN IGME's stillbirth rates are about 21 per 1,000 total births in sub-Saharan Africa and 20 in South Asia, lower elsewhere.

rows.label: Relative risk of stillbirth with community packages

source.title: Lassi & Bhutta (2015), Community-based intervention packages, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, doi:10.1002/14651858.CD007754.pub3
source.quote: stillbirths (average RR 0.81; 95% CI 0.73 to 0.91; 15 studies, n = 201,181

rows.explainer: The same review; the confidence interval as the range.

rows.label: Newborn deaths averted per birth covered
Stillbirths averted per birth covered
Value of a newborn death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The shared value of a neonatal death (@moral_weights.givewell_neonatal) × $life_value_multiplier.

rows.label: Value of a stillbirth averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The shared value (@givewell_shared.uov_per_stillbirth) × $life_value_multiplier.

rows.label: Life-satisfaction gain per survivor helped home (points on 0-10, per year)
rows.explainer: Judgment 0.8 (0.2-2). No study measures it. About half of trafficking survivors meet criteria for depression and 44% for PTSD (Karaahmet et al. 2026, meta-analysis of 18 studies, Archives of Women's Mental Health, doi:10.1007/s00737-026-01764-5; 71% and 61% among US survivors, Hopper et al. 2018); getting home to family and reintegration support relieve part of that, against staying stranded abroad.

rows.label: Years the gain lasts
rows.explainer: Judgment 2 (0.5-5): depression and PTSD after trafficking often last years; the help home relieves some of it for a while, not for good (0.5), or for several years once back with family (5).

rows.label: WELLBYs per survivor, discounted
Cash value of the supported services each person gets in a year
rows.explainer: Judgment $40 ($10-150): a child's share of a school's running costs, a few clinic visits, a place at a feeding programme.

rows.label: Consumption per person of the people the supported services reach (current US$ a year)
rows.explainer: Judgment $900 ($400-2,500). The money goes to territories that can't pay their own way, mostly in Africa and South Asia, and the services reach poor households there: the World Bank's extreme poverty line ($2.15 a day in 2017 prices) is about $500-900 a year at market rates in these countries, and the site's Bangladesh average is $1,819 (@bangladesh.consumption_per_person_2024).

rows.label: Gain in ln(consumption) per person served
Evidence adjustment, disaster relief
rows.explainer: 1: valued at its cash value, not from a study; down to 0.8 if goods were worth less locally than they cost.

rows.label: Share of the disaster relief outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 60% (30-90%): other agencies (UNHCR, the host governments, other NGOs) served the same refugees; the Ukraine response was better funded than most.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, livelihoods
rows.explainer: 0.8 (0.5-1): the effect comes from CARE's savings-group trials; SAWSO's livelihoods projects are other, smaller programmes run by church units, some of them income-generation and agriculture.

rows.label: Share of the livelihoods outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 1 (0.8-1): the trials' effects are against control villages, which already had their other options.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, education
rows.explainer: 0.6 (0.3-1): the effect is the median of evaluated programmes; these are small new projects (building work, dormitories, literacy centres) with no evaluation, and published effects run above what programmes do at scale.

rows.label: Share of the education outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 90% (60-100%): the effect is against the children's alternative in the studies; in the Pool Region up to half of children never enrol, so few would have had another place.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, health
rows.explainer: 0.4 (0.15-0.8): the trials' packages are community maternal and newborn care; SAWSO's health grants are a mix of clinics, community health, nursing training and other work, much of which isn't that package.

rows.label: Share of the health outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 1 (0.8-1): the trials' effects are against usual care, which already includes government clinics and other agencies; 0.8 where other programmes cover the same mothers.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, anti-trafficking
rows.explainer: 0.6 (0.3-1): the gain is a judgment from survivors' mental-health burden, not a measured effect of repatriation.

rows.label: Share of the anti-trafficking outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 50% (20-80%): embassies, IOM and other agencies repatriate survivors too; some would have got home without this help, later.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment, operating support
rows.explainer: 1 (0.7-1): valued at its cost, not from a study; how much of it becomes services and what they are worth are the rows above.

rows.label: Share of the operating support outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: 80% (50-100%): without the US money International Headquarters would have had less to share out; other territories and the recipient territories' own income would have replaced part of it.

rows.label: The US Salvation Army's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%). The US money pays for the projects; the local Salvation Army units deliver them with their own officers, buildings and volunteers, whose cost isn't in this model. Applied to every branch except anti-trafficking (its own share below).

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: SAWSO's share of the resources behind the repatriations
rows.explainer: Judgment 40% (15-80%). The count is the whole Salvation Army's, with SAWSO's support; flights average about $550 (report p. 14), and the $650,414 a year comes to about $1,300 per repatriation, with safe houses, embassies, IOM and the local Salvation Army adding their own resources.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (projects delivered as funded)
rows.explainer: Judgment 85% (60-100%): grants to church units in many countries, with SAWSO's project monitoring but no independent check; some money is delayed, diverted to other needs or lost. Every branch.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: 1 (0.85-1.05): SAWSO's grants rarely pull in others' money or free government money; some units would get the same from elsewhere (0.85). Every branch.

rows.label: Missing-data discount, disaster relief
rows.explainer: Thin: SAWSO publishes no count of people its relief reached; reach, value and counterfactual are judgments. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, livelihoods
rows.explainer: Thin: no count of members; the effect comes from trials of other programmes (CARE's savings groups). So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, education
rows.explainer: Thin: no count of children; the effect is the median of other programmes' evaluations. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, health
rows.explainer: Thin: no count of births covered; the effect comes from trials of community packages, not of these grants. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, anti-trafficking
rows.explainer: Thin: the repatriations are counted, but the gain is a judgment with no measurement. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Missing-data discount, operating support
rows.explainer: Thin: what the operating support becomes, and what it is worth, are judgments with no data. So it is counted less by the shared slider, the same way in every model (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined, disaster relief
rows.formula: relief_evidence_adj * relief_counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * relief_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's evidence, counterfactual and missing-data adjustments times the credit, delivery and funging adjustments.

rows.label: All adjustments combined, livelihoods
rows.formula: livelihood_evidence_adj * livelihood_counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * livelihood_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's evidence, counterfactual and missing-data adjustments times the credit, delivery and funging adjustments.

rows.label: All adjustments combined, education
rows.formula: education_evidence_adj * education_counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * education_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's evidence, counterfactual and missing-data adjustments times the credit, delivery and funging adjustments.

rows.label: All adjustments combined, health
rows.formula: health_evidence_adj * health_counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * health_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's evidence, counterfactual and missing-data adjustments times the credit, delivery and funging adjustments.

rows.label: All adjustments combined, anti-trafficking
rows.formula: trafficking_evidence_adj * trafficking_counterfactual_adj * trafficking_attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * trafficking_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The branch's evidence, counterfactual and missing-data adjustments times the credit, delivery and funging adjustments.

rows.label: All adjustments combined, operating support
rows.formula: support_evidence_adj * support_counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * support_missing_data_adj
